precepts.text: Herein do I exercise myself, to have always a conscience void of offence toward God, and toward men. What is better than standing up for God and standing up for his people? Getting your household in order, not committing fornication and adultery, taking care of your family. That is what better looks like.
precepts.point: Video played from a 1966 CBS documentary, Black Power, White Backlash, filmed in Cicero, Illinois, where 15,000 black people worked in the factories every day but not a single black family could live: residents said they would be afraid to go out at night, that you really could not trust any of them, and one said there are many good coloreds, but the ones that are going to march I don't like. They do not like when we march, because when we march we have our pride, our dignity, and our confidence. They do not like when we stand up as the nation of Israel; it angers them and it makes them afraid.

note.label: The Colossians & The CHRISTIANS of America

precepts.why:
Tatum said black people need to do better: y’all whole life is activism, y’all still complaining and protesting like y’all still slaves. Why were the brothers in Ocean Springs, Mississippi? Because one of our brothers, Nolan Wells, had a mysterious death with a bunch of white people around it, in a town known for lynching black people. Yes, we are activists. Yes, we stand up for righteousness and speak against the evils and atrocities that happen to our people. That puts fear in our oppressors, and he is doing their bidding: hey, you’ve been cooning great lately.

So what is better than standing up for God and standing up for his people? “And herein do I exercise myself, to have always a conscience void of offence toward God, and toward men.”

We always have to do what is right toward God and toward our people. Better looks like getting your household in order, not committing fornication and adultery, taking care of your family. What is better than that? That is what a conscience void of offence looks like, and he is not speaking from the point of a black man.

precepts.text: Paul exercised himself to always have a conscience void of offence toward God and toward men, just as Daniel did.
precepts.point: This is how our forefathers rolled, and the same kind of spirit we should be rolling in. They concluded they could only find something against him concerning the law of his God.

note.label: Daniel 6: Daniel in the Den of Lions

precepts.why:
“And herein do I exercise myself, to have always a conscience void of offence toward God, and toward men.” Paul exercised himself at it, worked at it, so that neither God nor men could find offence in him. That is exactly what Daniel did. The presidents and princes sought occasion against him concerning the kingdom, “but they could find none occasion nor fault; forasmuch as he was faithful, neither was there any error or fault found in him.” He was blameless: void of offence toward men in the affairs of the kingdom, and void of offence toward God in keeping his law.

The only thing left for them to try was the law of his God: “We shall not find any occasion against this Daniel, except we find it against him concerning the law of his God.” There was nothing else on him.

This is how our forefathers rolled, and the same kind of spirit we should be rolling in: exercising ourselves, as Daniel and Paul did, to have always a conscience void of offence toward God and toward men.

precepts.text: Paul was accused as a mover of sedition among all the Jews throughout the world, showing Israel was scattered worldwide.
precepts.point: The historical record in A Tribute to the Negro says the Jews, though their features assimilated to the nations among whom they were scattered, descended from one stock, were forbidden to intermarry, and yet according to the divine prediction were dispersed into every country, marked with the colors of all: brown and swarthy in Turkey and Portugal, black in Spain, Syria, Chaldea, Arabia, Egypt, and at the Congo in Africa. Swarthy means dark and black, tawny means copper or brown, and olive is not "all colors," for a man of all colors would be a diseased spectacle, not a real man; Christ was black and brown.

note.label: Acts 2: Pentecost and the Scattered House of Israel

precepts.why:
Paul's accusers called him “a mover of sedition among all the Jews throughout the world”. The Jews were throughout the world. Israel had been scattered into all the kingdoms of the earth, which is why devout men, men who kept the laws, were dwelling at Jerusalem out of every nation under heaven.

Only one race of people was prophesied to be dispersed to every country. That is the reason men from every nation were present at Pentecost.

They call it heresy because it is not according to their standard: they have a Christmas tree up and celebrate all the man-made holidays. Paul confessed, “that after the way which they call heresy, so worship I the God of my fathers, believing all things which are written in the law and in the prophets”. We believe and exercise the things written in the law and the prophets.

“And herein do I exercise myself, to have always a conscience void of offence toward God, and toward men.” That is how brothers keep a good name on their jobs while the world calls the faith false. We are not trying to offend people; we are just trying to live a peaceable life by keeping the commandments of the Lord.

note.label: THE BLACK BOULÉ & BOURGEOISIE IN THE BIBLE

precepts.why: “Now after many years I came to bring alms to my nation, and offerings.” Paul’s alms were for his nation.

note.label: Unlocking The Three Angels Prophecies And More

precepts.why: “But this I confess unto thee, that after the way which they call heresy”. So the teachings of Christ were called a heresy. So don’t feel upset when they say you’re in a cult. Don’t feel no way, because they said Christ perverted the nation and his teachings were heresy. They say the same about us today.

“But we desire to hear of thee what thou thinkest: for as concerning this sect”, that cult, “we know that every where it is spoken against.”

Why? Why do the heathen rage and the people imagine a vain thing. As it was back then, so it is today: the followers of Christ are called a cult and spoken against everywhere.

points: Paul exercised himself to have always a conscience void of offence toward God and men. That is the greatest commandment: love God and love your neighbour.
that after the way which they call heresy, so worship I the God of my fathers: let's see. Did Paul change anything?

believing all things which are written in the law: whoa, whoa, whoa, whoa. He said, me believing the law and keeping the law, they call it heresy. Ain't that what they do with the Israelites? They say y'all are in a cult because you are adhering to the law, statutes, and commandments. The only laws we do not keep are the temple laws, sacrificing. Christ did away with that. But we don't steal. We don't kill. We don't eat pork. But they'll say that those are being too strict, too harsh.
and in the prophets: so believing all things. Christians don't believe all things.

If none of this is true, and what we teach is heresy, they wouldn’t go to these great lengths and spend all this money. “And when Felix heard these things, having more perfect knowledge of that way”: like Katt Williams said, the liar knows the lie he told. Felix knew exactly what Paul was teaching.
“He sent for Paul, and heard him concerning the faith in Christ.” He knew about that way, and he wanted to hear it.

“And as he reasoned of righteousness, temperance, and judgment to come, Felix trembled”. Paul told him of righteousness, the commandments, of temperance, and of the judgment to come. If the judgment Paul taught were foolishness, like a black man coming out of the sky, Felix would have said, you’re just crazy. Instead he trembled. That is why Esau is crazy over us on the street corners: he hears Revelation 2:9 and it clicks, I have to get payback. As James said, the devils also believe, and tremble.
“For we have found this man a pestilent fellow, and a mover of sedition among all the Jews throughout the world, and a ringleader of the sect of the Nazarenes”: that is talking about Christ.

Sect is a group of people with somewhat different religious beliefs, typically regarded as heretical by the larger group to which they belong; and a word similar to it is cult. That’s what they said: oh, they’re a cult, these guys are a cult. Sect and cult are the same thing. That’s what Acts 24 is saying: a ringleader of the sect, or cult, of the Nazarenes.
